models.model_label: Table 7 Panel A Model 3: full cross-sectional regression of implied risk premium
models.sample_description: Annual June 30 cross-sections of NYSE and AMEX stocks with available data, 1979–1995. The main sample requires CRSP/Compustat coverage, required accounting and market data, and one- and two-year-ahead I/B/E/S EPS forecasts. The paper reports annual firm counts from 1,018 to 1,333, but not the exact N for each annual fit.
models.method_details: The authors report annual Fama–MacBeth regressions. The underlying estimator for each annual cross-sectional fit is not identified in the paper.

dependent_variable.name: r_i,t − r_f,t (implied risk premium)
dependent_variable.definition: Annualized year-t implied risk premium for firm i, measured in percent as the firm-specific internal rate of return from a 12-year Edwards–Bell–Ohlson residual-income valuation less the end-of-month yield on a 10-year Treasury bond. The valuation equates the June 30 stock price to beginning book value per share plus discounted residual income and a terminal value. It uses I/B/E/S mean EPS forecasts for years 1 and 2; year-3 EPS is forecast as year-2 EPS times (1+Ltg), using the growth implicit in FY1 and FY2 when Ltg is unavailable. ROE is forecast explicitly for the first three years, then linearly mean-reverted to a moving median ROE for profitable firms in the same Fama–French 48 industry, calculated from at least five and up to ten past years; reported results use T=12 and a terminal value beyond T. Future book values use clean-surplus accounting, with dividends based on the latest fiscal-year payout ratio; the payout ratio excludes share repurchases, divides dividends by earnings (or by 0.06 times total assets when earnings are negative), and is bounded to [0,1]. Until reported book value becomes available four months after fiscal year-end, book value is forecast using prior book value plus earnings less dividends; thereafter the actual Compustat value is used.
dependent_variable.formula: r_e solved from the 12-year EBO price equation − end-of-month 10-year Treasury yield, as of June 30

evidence.quote: Equation(5): P_t = B_t + ((FROE_(t+1)-r_e)/(1+r_e))*B_t + ((FROE_(t+2)-r_e)/(1+r_e)^2)*B_(t+1) + TV. Equation(6): TV = sum_(i=3)^(T-1) [((FROE_(t+i)-r_e)/(1+r_e)^i)*B_(t+i-1)] + ((FROE_(t+T)-r_e)/(r_e*(1+r_e)^(T-1)))*B_(t+T-1). T=12 in reported results.
The reported horizon is T=12. Industry target ROE is the moving median of past ROEs from profitable firms in the same Fama-French48 industry, using at least five and up to ten past years.

First/two-year-ahead forecasts are IBES mean EPS; year3 forecast is FEPS_(t+2)*(1+Ltg). When Ltg is missing (including before1981), use the growth implicit in the year1/year2 forecasts to forecast year3.
From announcement month through four months after fiscal year-end, synthetic B_t=B_(t-1)+EPS_t-D_t; after the fourth month use actual reported Compustat book value as continued on page11.

Expected payout k is latest-fiscal-year actual dividends divided by earnings for that period, excluding share repurchases. For negative earnings, use dividends/(0.06*totalAssets). Set payout below0 to0 and above1 to1.

We estimate the IRR for each firm at the end ofJune each year by substituting the forecasted future earnings, book values, and terminal values into equation (5) and solving the resulting non-linear equation. We then subtract the end-of-month yield on long-term (10-year) Treasury bonds from the IRR measure to obtain an (annualized) implied risk premium for each firm in the sample.
Response is the firm’s implied risk premium derived from the twelve-year EBO model in percent.
